gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Furbo's own checkout turns the $35 Furbo Mini 360° into $118.92 on day one ($35 + $83.92 Furbo Nanny billed up front), or that Petcube's $0-camera Bites 2 Lite bundle locks in $119.88 for year one ($9.99 × a 12-month minimum). Both are over the shopper's $100 cap. The TKENPRO 2K costs $85.49–$89.99 on Amazon and records to microSD, so it stays under $100 even with video history.
standout_why: VettedFur (cited) works out year-one cost with the plan only for the Petcube Bites 2 Lite bought outright ($79.99 + $59.88 = $139.87) and for the full-size Furbo 360° ($267.92). It lists the Furbo Mini 360° as out of stock with no price, and it doesn't mention Petcube's 12-month bundle commitment. TheConsumers.guide (cited) says outright that it gives no plan prices, so its 'total cost' is just the camera price. WIRED was unreachable to my fetch tool. PawCog failed on a certificate error. ChatGPT itself showed the Furbo Mini 360° as '$30–49' and as fitting under $100, adding only that 'some discounted offers' need Nanny. It never gave the checkout total.
decides: It confirms the Petcube Bites 2 Lite as the pick for a shopper who wants no plan ($79.99 on Amazon for live view, talk and treats). It removes the Furbo Mini 360° from 'under $100': Furbo's own cart is $118.92, and Furbo's terms set a 3-month minimum with no refunds. It also adds a line the rivals lack: if the shopper wants recorded clips in year one for under $100, only the TKENPRO 2K qualifies ($85.49–$89.99, microSD). Petcube with history is at least $119.88 (bundle) or $139.87 (outright plus Optimal).
